The Prophet tested the boy Ibn Saiyad and refused Umar leave to kill him, saying the Dajjal could not be overpowered; he later tried to overhear him.
Angels guard Medina from plague and the Dajjal; it will shake out disbelievers and hypocrites; outside it the Dajjal will kill and revive a believer, but cannot repeat it.
Hiding behind palms to hear Ibn Saiyyad murmur under a sheet, the Prophet says that had his mother not alerted him, the truth would have been clear.
The Prophet tests young Ibn Saiyad and stops Umar killing him; later he warns that the Dajjal, of whom every prophet warned, is one-eyed, and Allah is not.
Every prophet, Noah among them, warned his nation of the Dajjal, but the Prophet adds that he is one-eyed, unlike Allah, and his Paradise will really be Hell.
The Prophet tested the boy Ibn Saiyad, who answered 'Ad-Dukh', refused Umar leave to kill him, tried to overhear him, and warned that the Dajjal is one-eyed, unlike Allah.
The Prophet told Ibn Saiyad he could not exceed his limits and stopped Umar killing him: if he were the Dajjal Umar could not overcome him, otherwise killing gained nothing.
Every prophet warned of the one-eyed Dajjal, marked 'Kafir', whose fire is water; he will kill and revive a man, but angels will keep him and plague out of Medina.
Jabir swore that Ibn Sayyad was the Dajjal, because Umar had sworn so before the Prophet and the Prophet did not object.
Allah is not one-eyed, while the Dajjal, of whom every prophet warned, is blind in the right eye with 'Kafir' written between his eyes.
